vignette: A 36-year-old woman, a migrant worker living in Zhongshan, Guangdong Province, has had fever, fatigue, joint swelling and weight loss for nine months. Another hospital diagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus and treated her with steroids and several immunosuppressants without benefit. She is admitted with high spiking fevers ten days after stopping prednisone and cyclosporine herself.
opening_statement_lay: I've had fevers on and off for about nine months, and I'm worn out and much thinner. The lupus treatment never really helped, and since I stopped my tablets the high fevers have come back.

facts.release_text: Fever, fatigue, joint swelling and weight loss for nine months.
Fever for nine months, at times spiking to 40 °C, with profound fatigue and significant weight loss.

The illness has worsened over nine months. On steroids and immunosuppressants a low-grade fever persisted and the blood counts improved very little. Ten days after she stopped prednisone and cyclosporine herself, high spiking fevers returned.
Joint swelling during the illness; the joints involved are not recorded.
Asthma for four years, never treated. No other past medical history.
No contact with anyone with a fever.
A migrant worker who lives and works in Zhongshan, Guangdong Province, with her husband. Type of work not recorded.
Her husband is well. No family history of recurrent or unusual infections.

facts.release_text: Records from a local hospital in Zhongshan, early in the illness: haemoglobin 91 g/L, white cells 2.0 x10^9/L, platelets 73 x10^9/L; CRP 35 mg/L, ESR 59 mm/h, ferritin 256 ug/L; ANA positive at 1:320 and anti-mitochondrial M2 antibody positive; IgG 53 g/L; liver and renal function normal; serum and urine immunofixation normal. Bone marrow examination was reported as a hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia and no evidence of malignancy or parasites. CT of the abdomen showed an enlarged liver and spleen.

Discharge summary from the rheumatology department of a tertiary hospital, where she was admitted when the fever rose to 40 °C: pancytopenia; polyclonal gammopathy; ANA 1:320; anti-dsDNA and anti-PM-Scl antibodies positive; direct antiglobulin test positive; low C3 and C4. Ultrasound showed an enlarged liver and spleen, the spleen 25 cm in its long axis. Repeat bone marrow smears and biopsy were reported as showing nothing diagnostic. Diagnosis: systemic lupus erythematosus.

Treated for systemic lupus erythematosus with high-dose glucocorticoids, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib and telitacicept (a BLyS/APRIL inhibitor). The fever persisted at a low grade and the blood counts improved very little.
Prednisone had been tapered to 20 mg daily, with cyclosporine 50 mg twice daily. She stopped both herself ten days before admission.

raw_material.findings: Giemsa-stained aspirate smears show intracellular Leishmania amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) within marrow macrophages, seen at 400x and 1000x. Specimen preparation and staining followed the national standard for smear microscopy (WS/T 10018-2024); the finding was confirmed by the national reference laboratory. Background marrow cellularity and other lineages are not described.
raw_material.note: Day of the aspirate not stated; placed on day 0. Two earlier marrows at other hospitals were reported without parasites (H12, H13).

final_diagnosis.text: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) acquired in her endemic home province (Shanxi), misdiagnosed as systemic lupus erythematosus because of autoantibodies, a positive direct antiglobulin test, hypocomplementaemia and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia

final_dx.text: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) acquired in her endemic home province (Shanxi), misdiagnosed as systemic lupus erythematosus because of autoantibodies, a positive direct antiglobulin test, hypocomplementaemia and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia

secondary_findings: ANA 1:160-1:320, anti-dsDNA (earlier), anti-PM-Scl, anti-M2 and a positive DAT with low C3: autoantibodies from polyclonal B-cell activation in the infection, not lupus
Pancytopenia from splenic pooling and marrow parasitisation, with an inadequate reticulocyte response
Low-level EBV DNA under immunosuppression: an incidental reactivation
Probable adrenal suppression after abrupt withdrawal of long-term prednisone
accepted_differential: Chronic liver disease with portal hypertension and hypersplenism
Myelofibrosis or chronic myeloid leukaemia (massive spleen)
red_herrings: anti-dsDNA positive at the other hospital
living and working in a non-endemic province
key_discriminators: home town in Shanxi with regular travel there
anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm negative at this admission
ground_truth.treatment_given: Liposomal amphotericin B 1.3 mg/kg daily, extended to 30 days because of the long illness and prior immunosuppression; immunosuppression stopped; confirmation by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention.
ground_truth.outcome: Fever settled within 48 hours; counts normal 21 days after discharge; marrow and PCR negative three weeks after treatment; spleen 16.6 cm at four months. Discharged well in March 2025.
teaching_points: Ask every migrant worker where they come from and how often they go home: the endemic exposure may be far from where they live and work.
A spleen over 20 cm is very unusual in lupus; look for infection, a haematological cancer or portal hypertension.
ANA, anti-dsDNA, low complement and a positive DAT occur in visceral leishmaniasis; autoantibodies never outweigh clinicopathological correlation.
Failure of intensive immunosuppression argues against the autoimmune diagnosis, and immunosuppression worsens an unrecognised infection.

A negative marrow does not exclude the diagnosis: repeat it and ask for a specific search, or use rK39 and PCR. Splenic aspiration is the most sensitive but is contraindicated with very low platelets.
Liposomal amphotericin B is first-line; test for HIV and notify public health.

must_do.text: Take a full residence and travel history, including her home province and visits home
Look for the parasite directly: a repeat bone marrow aspirate examined for amastigotes, or Leishmania PCR, despite the two earlier negative marrows
Arrange follow-up for response and relapse (counts, spleen size, test of cure)

must_not_do.text: Restart or escalate immunosuppression for presumed lupus
Commit to lupus without a parasitological work-up despite a massive spleen and failure of intensive immunosuppression
Splenectomy for the cytopenias or the spleen
Splenic aspiration while platelets are 29 x10^9/L and the PT is prolonged

gaps.guidance: High spiking fever (the reason for admission); tachycardia from fever and Hb 59 g/L; blood pressure low-normal; SpO2 normal.
Massive, firm, non-tender spleen consistent with 25.9 cm on CT; liver palpable; no ascites reported.
Pallor; thin after significant weight loss; mild ankle oedema possible with albumin 20 g/L; no rash or synovitis reported; no significant lymphadenopathy reported.

gaps.item: rK39 rapid test (not done in the article)
gaps.guidance: Likely positive in active disease; sensitivity may be lower after months of immunosuppression.

gaps.item: Complete blood count indices and reticulocytes on day 0
gaps.guidance: Normocytic anaemia; reticulocyte response inadequate for Hb 59 g/L; monocytes and basophils must make the differential sum to 0.87 x10^9/L.
DAT positive from polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia; at most mild haemolysis (LDH 284 U/L).
Raised triglycerides and soluble CD25 are common in active disease; the article does not report them or HLH. Keep below the HLH-2004 thresholds.

gaps.item: Bone marrow trephine and other marrow studies at this admission
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Reactive, plasma-cell rich marrow; no lymphoma or clonal process.
